newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO DRAW, HAVE LEAD CUT TO FOUR AS PSG WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO DRAW, HAVE LEAD CUT TO FOUR AS PSG WIN.

text.p: Monaco's lead in the French first division was cut to four points on Sunday as Paris St Germain, scoring twice in the last three minutes, came from behind to beat 10-man Lyon 3-1 for their first home win in four months.
The leaders dropped two points when they were held to a 0-0 draw at home by defending champions Auxerre but maintained the only unbeaten home record in the top flight this season.
Auxerre striker Lilian Laslandes had a shot turned on to the post by Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez in the 49th minute after he had broken through the middle of the defence.
Laslandes just beat Barthez to the rebound but blasted his second effort over the bar.
At the other end 10 minutes later, Monaco teenager Thierry Henry put the ball just wide after Brazilian Anderson headed the ball down into his path.
Laslandes, whose team climbed one place to seventh though they remain 13 points behind Monaco, said: "We're still up among the leaders and with a chance of qualifying (for Europe)."

In Paris, PSG captain Rai scored twice, first heading his side level at 1-1 two minutes into the second half from a corner by fellow Brazilian Leonardo after striker Cedric Bardon had put Lyon ahead in the 10th minute.

France striker Patrice Loko put PSG ahead in the 87th minute from a cross from the left by Leonardo and Rai headed the third a minute later. Loko and Rai have now scored eight goals each in the league this season.
Lyon defender Florent Laville was sent off midway through the second half for a second bookable offence.
Earlier centre back Bruno N'Gotty headed against the Lyon crossbar and goalkeeper Bernard Lama made a crucial save with his foot from striker Alain Caveglia, the visitors' top scorer.
PSG had not won at the Parc des Princes in six league games and two European matches since beating Lille 3-1 on November 13.
"We just have to keep battling away," PSG president Michel Denisot said.
PSG sank into deep crisis after a home loss to relegation candidates Nancy in December and a 6-1 drubbing by Juventus in the first leg of the European Super Cup in January.
The European Cup Winners' Cup holders were also held 0-0 at home by AEK Athens in the first leg of a quarter-final tie on Thursday, failing to translate territorial dominance into goals.
On Saturday, Nantes extended their unbeaten league run to 21 games when they beat third-placed Bastia 3-0 at home. The win enhanced sixth-placed Nantes' hopes of a berth in Europe next season.
